reviews.reason: Portable protection is not equivalent to the fixed shelter or energy-consuming active warming. A woven, overlapping bark mantle secured with vines can provide modest wind and cold protection while moving, without generating heat. Materials must actually be obtained: the observed vines are potential inputs, but no bark or completed garment is currently owned. Missing inputs do not invalidate development.
reviews.experienceReview: Actual reduction of personally experienced cold discomfort can provide modest relief; manufacturing, ownership, learning and application cannot. Add insulation-comfort-qualified as an alternative trigger of the existing thermal-refuge source, not a new aliased source. For the wearer only, qualify after three consecutive equipped rounds with positive measured avoided cooling and lower cold discomfort than the same-round unprotected calculation, with no starvation or health loss. Emit at most one qualification per completed three-round block; source awards remain 1, cap 1, duration 6 rounds and shared cooldown 12 rounds across shelter, exercise and mantle triggers. Repeated qualifying use is legitimate but never stacks awards. This provides temporary relief only: it does not independently increase sustained mental state, award achievement satisfaction or modify protected mental accounts. Physical comfort continues to use actual temperature, hunger, fatigue and health.
reviews.visualReview: Render overlapping bark panels and vine ties on the actual equipped actor, with visible darkening as wetness increases and fraying as condition decreases. Ground and inventory views show the same persistent item identity. Craft and repair replay shows paid rounds and actual inputs reserved or consumed; cancellation shows surviving material released once. Exposure events display avoided cooling beside remaining cooling and net temperature change, without implying warmth generation, immunity or a room. Equipment changes and wear-out are replayable from declared events, not cosmetic labels standing in for protection.
reviews.specification:
Implement portable-insulation@1 through the current conversation handoff. Public interface portable-insulation has a strict object schema: mode enum craft/equip/unequip/repair, target optional string maxLength 1000; target forbidden for craft and required otherwise; no additional properties. Shared references use item:ID for exact instances and resource:ID for owned categories, with existing compatibility aliases and ambiguity reporting. Resolve and retain exact identities throughout an operation. Prerequisites: personal study of this interface; crafting additionally requires 4 owned bark units and 2 owned vine units. No tools, fire, supplied stock or pre-existing garment are assumed. Executable precursor is hand-overlapping flexible bark panels and weaving vine ties, not merely carrying raw materials. Craft takes 5 consecutive stationary rounds at 1.5 energy each, with normal metabolism. Reserve actual inputs in actor-owned escrow; they retain identity and aging and cannot be spent elsewhere. Completion atomically consumes surviving required inputs and creates one unequipped mantle with their mass, provenance and moisture. Persist owner, equipment slot, condition 0–160, moisture 0–1, repair provenance and last processed tick. Equip/unequip each takes one round and 0.5 energy; only the living owner can equip an owned mantle, with one mantle slot. Dropping or giving it first unequips it. Repair an unequipped owned mantle with 2 bark and 1 vine over 2 stationary rounds at 1 energy each; consume escrow only on completion, restoring condition to 160, not adding beyond it. Retain input/output mass accounting: repair removes an equal mass of worn panels as non-edible scrap, rather than deleting material or accumulating unbounded garment mass.
Physical mechanism: integrate the equipped mantle into the existing temperature/exposure solver. For condition c>0 and moisture m, multiply only the below-comfort environmental cooling component by 1-((0.25-0.15*m)*min(1,c/40)). This is passive wind resistance and trapped-air insulation, never heat production; combine multiplicatively with applicable shelter protection without applying either twice. Leave warm-weather exposure, hunger, health and rest rules unchanged. Update moisture once per actual world round: +0.10 when directly exposed to rain, otherwise -0.02, clamped to [0,1]; use actual shelter/weather geometry to determine rain exposure. Lose one condition per equipped round; zero condition provides no protection. Carried but unequipped garments provide none. Include garment and escrow mass in existing carrying costs. Record pre-protection cooling, avoided cooling, actual net temperature change and remaining exposure; temperature may still fall.
Geometry and execution: worn geometry follows the carrier and does not create a shelter, obstacle or larger interaction reach. Unequipped ground garments use shared item placement, pickup reach and collision rules, never obsolete pickup coordinates. Each work round validates life, ownership, stationary position, energy and surviving inputs. Persist completed rounds and actual remaining work. Action changes, death or invalidation cancel unfinished work, retaining paid effort and returning surviving unconsumed escrow exactly once to its existing owner inventory or that owner's death-drop location; never clone, silently delete or refund consumed materials. Global pauses preserve progress and advance no time. Repeat counts complete operations. Emit and register insulation-started, insulation-progress, insulation-completed, insulation-cancelled, insulation-equipped, insulation-unequipped, insulation-exposure-measured, insulation-worn-out and insulation-comfort-qualified. Events carry actor/item identities, paid costs, remaining work, condition, moisture, input provenance and measured physical deltas as applicable. Bind task and memory adapters to these events. Migrate additively with empty equipment slots and no generated items, mastery or retroactive awards; existing sources and history remain intact.

satisfactionSources.name: Cautious food relief
satisfactionSources.rationale: Modest relief follows personally experienced nourishment from completed monitored exposure without adverse or confounding evidence. Examination, labels and absence of evidence do not certify safety or earn reward.

satisfactionSources.name: Thermal refuge
satisfactionSources.rationale: Three consecutive stationary resting/waiting rounds with measured avoided cold loss and lower cold discomfort, without starvation or health loss. Ownership, construction, application and study alone do not qualify.

request.name: Portable cold protection
request.function: Make and use portable insulation to reduce actual cold exposure while travelling and resting outdoors.
request.conditions: At tick 444 I am outdoors in autumn rain and wind, with ambient temperature 9.93, body temperature 14.94 and health 100. Exercise raised temperature only about 0.18 per round at a cost of 3 energy. Nearby observed materials include branches, vines and resin. The implemented shelter requires dry-grass, which I have not located.
request.inputs: Suitable materials and construction method are unknown; determine feasible inputs from real obtainable materials without granting them automatically.
request.costs: Unknown; require actual materials, learning and work, with durability or maintenance if appropriate.
request.effects: Measurably reduce cold-related temperature loss while worn or carried as appropriate. No automatic heat, healing, immunity or satisfaction; report actual protection and remaining exposure.
